authoredPrompt: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate one full MDP time step: sequentially highlight state s_t leaving the Environment → entering the Agent → action a_t flowing back → reward r_{t+1} and next state s_{t+1} returned from the Environment
- Click the Agent box to highlight the policy π[a_t|s_t] and the action arrow a_t pointing toward the environment
- Click the Environment box to highlight both the state transition Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) and the reward function Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) labels

discrepancies: The four edge labels that sit on the vertical arrows in the source — 'Reward rₜ' (leftmost), 'State sₜ' (inner left), 'State sₜ' (inner right), 'Action aₜ' (rightmost) — are not visible in the render; the arrows instead show blank white gaps where the label text should be.
The 'sₜ₊₁' and 'rₜ₊₁' annotations next to the dashed time-step boundary on the left are not visible in the render.
The policy label reads 'π[aₜ|s]' instead of the source's 'π[aₜ|sₜ]' (the subscript t on the conditioning state is dropped).

In the source the vertical arrows are continuous lines with labels overlaid on top; the generated arrows are broken into two segments separated by an empty white rectangle, changing the visual character of the loop.
evaluation.notes: The two-box MDP topology, teal/orange color scheme, arrow directions, dashed time-step line, and the step-player/click-popup interactions are all correct and pedagogically sound, but the figure fails as a drop-in replacement because the four on-arrow edge labels (Reward/State/State/Action) and the sₜ₊₁/rₜ₊₁ annotations do not appear in the render, leaving blank gaps in the arrows.
action_items: Fix the label() helper so the edge-label text actually renders: the white background rect is drawn but the text is invisible, producing empty gaps in the arrows. Ensure the text node is appended after the rect with a visible fill and correct baseline (e.g. use t.attr({x:cx, y:cy, 'dominant-baseline':'middle'}) or compute bbox after the font is applied), and confirm 'Reward rₜ', 'State sₜ', 'State sₜ', 'Action aₜ' all show.
Make the 'sₜ₊₁' and 'rₜ₊₁' labels beside the dashed line visible (same label-rendering fix); they are currently absent from the screenshot.
Correct the policy text to 'π[aₜ|sₜ]' (add the missing subscript t on the conditioning state) to match the source.

Draw the vertical arrows as continuous polylines and place the labels on top of them (with a small white halo) rather than splitting each arrow into two segments with an empty white rectangle in the middle.

feedback.rationale: The concept, topology, and interactivity are all correct (scores of 4), but the generator has a text-rendering bug causing edge labels to be invisible, a missing subscript, and broken arrow segments — all concrete implementation fixes that don't require replanning.
